newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh savings bonds raise about $4.4 mln - official.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh savings bonds raise about $4.4 mln - official.

text.p: The first issue of Kazakh National Savings Bonds (NSOs), for which subscriptions ended last week, raised about 300 million tenge ($4.4 million), a government official said on Monday.
"The final results of the issue will be known on Wednesday, when the money will be transferred to the budget," a Finance Ministry source told Reuters.
Narodny Bank, the former state savings bank, and Kazkommertsbank had to place NSOs worth 200 million and 100 million tenge respectively.
The 364-day bonds, with a nominal value of 1,000 tenge and issued on September 11, aimed to attract small investors, looking for ways to secure their cash savings.
Narodny Bank has said Kazakhstan's 17 million people were holding about $1 billion in cash, with many preferring to keep their savings under the mattress rather than trust volitile financial markets.
Finance Ministry officials say the bonds were sold all over Kazakhstan, as private persons rushed to subscribe to the paper.

The first quarterly coupon of the bonds, whose returns are pegged to yields of Kazakh three-month Treasury bills, will pay 27.4 percent annual, while bank accounts offer fixed returns of four to 25 percent annual.
The largest sum paid for the NSOs by a single private subscriber was one million tenge, a Narodny Bank official said.
